title: Universal simulation for a fixed number of tapes
statement: For every natural number $k$ and every effective coding scheme $E$ for machines with $k$ work tapes, there is a finite binary-alphabet Turing machine $U$ such that, for each code $\alpha$, there is a natural number $C$ for which the following holds for every Boolean input word $x$. If the machine decoded from $\alpha$ produces output $y$ and halts on $x$ after exactly $t$ steps, then $U$ produces $y$ and halts on $\langle\alpha,x\rangle$ after exactly $C(t+1)$ steps; conversely, if $U$ produces $y$ and halts on $\langle\alpha,x\rangle$, then the machine decoded from $\alpha$ produces $y$ and halts on $x$ after some number of steps.
hypotheses_covered: $E$ is an effective coding scheme for $k$-work-tape machines
replaced:
For every number $k$ of work tapes and every effective coding scheme for $k$-tape
machines, there is a finite binary-alphabet Turing machine $U$ with the following
property. For each code $\alpha$, there is a constant $C\in\mathbb{N}$ such that for
every input $x$, (i) whenever the machine decoded from $\alpha$ produces output $y$ and
halts after exactly $t$ steps on $x$, $U$ produces the same output on
$\langle\alpha,x\rangle$ and halts after exactly $C(t+1)$ steps; and (ii) whenever $U$
produces output $y$ and halts on $\langle\alpha,x\rangle$, the machine decoded from
$\alpha$ produces $y$ and halts on $x$ after some number of steps.
